title: FEAT- Mobile Phase 0: Platform prerequisites for native clients
description: Backend work required before an Expo client can exist: native session transport, device tokens and push delivery, and GraphQL codegen. Complete and verified; go build, go vet and go test ./... pass.

title: FEAT- Native session transport (X-Client header, refresh token in body)
description: Clients sending X-Client: mobile/native/api receive refresh_token and refresh_expires_in alongside the access token on login and refresh. Header-based rather than User-Agent so a browser cannot be talked into exposing its refresh token to JavaScript.

title: FEAT- Return rotated refresh token to body-token clients on /auth/refresh
description: Without returning the new refresh token, a native client's second refresh replays a spent token, trips the reuse detector and revokes the session it was renewing.

title: FEAT- Accept refresh token from cookie, X-Refresh-Token header or JSON body
description: presentedRefreshToken resolves in that order so refresh and logout work without a cookie jar.

title: FEAT- DeviceToken model (one row per install, keyed on push token)
description: Push token is the device identity. Re-registering an existing token reassigns it to the new user, which stops a shared ward tablet delivering the previous nurse's alerts to the next one.

title: FEAT- Expo push delivery client with chunking and dead-token cleanup
description: push.Client chunks to Expo's 100-message limit, parses per-message errors from the HTTP 200 body, and disables DeviceNotRegistered tokens so the table does not fill with dead entries.

title: FEAT- push.NotifyRecord fan-out at the three notification creation sites
description: Single entry point; delivery runs on its own goroutine and errors are logged, never returned, so a push outage cannot fail the mutation that triggered it.

title: FEAT- Lock-screen push redaction (summary and deep link only)
description: Notification bodies can name a patient or a result and render on a locked phone in a public corridor. Full text is read in-app behind auth.

title: FEAT- GraphQL registerDeviceToken / revokeDeviceToken / myDeviceTokens
description: Self-service and caller-scoped, so deliberately absent from opAccess like the other my* operations. The push token is a delivery credential and is never returned by the API.

title: FEAT- Disable device tokens on password change and delete with the user account
description: Device tokens follow revoked sessions.

title: CHORE- GraphQL codegen from committed schema (frontend/codegen.ts)
description: Generates frontend/types/graphql.ts from backend/graph/schema.graphqls and every document under graphql/. Reads the schema from the repo rather than introspecting a running server, so it works in CI and the mobile client consumes the same committed types without a Go toolchain.

title: BUG: upsertCalendarDay selects weekday on Holiday, server rejects at validation
description: weekday belongs to CalendarDay; Holiday has never had it, so the mutation could not have worked. The caller in calendarSlice.ts discards the result, so the fix was to select fields that exist. Found by codegen validation.

title: BUG: Two different ListCourses queries sharing one operation name
description: academic.ts (plain list) and students.ts (with batches) collided. Second renamed to ListCoursesWithBatches; exported constant unchanged so no import site moved. Tolerated by Apollo but breaks persisted queries and operation allowlisting.

title: BUG: GetAttendanceSettings defined twice, identically, in two files
description: attendance.ts and calendar.ts both defined it; calendar.ts now re-exports the single definition.

title: CHORE- Wire gen:graphql:check into CI to fail on stale codegen output
description: npm run gen:graphql:check already exists and fails on stale output. Not yet wired into CI. Note: this repo uses pnpm and the three @graphql-codegen/* devDependencies are in package.json but not installed.

title: BUG: backend/ and frontend/ are gitlinks, so their changes are unversioned
description: Both are recorded in git as gitlinks (mode 160000) with no .gitmodules and no .git directory of their own, so git status at the root reports nothing when their files change. Everything built so far is unversioned on disk. Fix before any further work lands.

title: BUG: deactivateUser does not revoke refresh tokens or device tokens
description: deactivateUser marks the user inactive but leaves refresh tokens live. middleware.Authenticate catches it on the next access token, so the window is one access-token lifetime rather than indefinite, but it should call RevokeUserSessions and DisableUserDeviceTokens outright. Pre-existing, unrelated to mobile.

title: FEAT- Active sessions list and admin remote sign-out
